lines.story: SBP is holding at 12.0% -- Red zone. After inflation, savers earn +2.4pp in real terms -- money stays expensive, favouring banks and cash-rich names over leveraged cyclicals.
CPI at 9.6% is below the 11% defensive trigger -- the inflation tilt is OFF; the defensive stance is rate-driven, not price-driven.
Rupee near 276 with REER at 110.6 -- above 100 means the rupee is rich vs trading partners; devaluation pressure builds slowly rather than imminently.
SBP reserves of $21.6B cover about 3.3 months of imports -- at/above the 3-month adequacy line.
current account +0.0B USD (surplus helps reserves); fiscal deficit ~2.6% of GDP.

netbenefits.plain_summary: What Zacks says after the 5 November report, in plain language: APD delivered the quarter. Adjusted earnings of $3.61 a share beat the $3.60 expected by a whisker and were up from $3.39 a year ago; that makes four beats in the last four quarters (the one before was $3.47 against $3.36, a 3.3% beat). Sales of $3.56 billion were 12.3% higher than last year's $3.17 billion and 7.2% above what analysts expected, with the Americas doing the heavy lifting (+26.7%) while Asia and Europe came in a little under estimates. The stock is up 29.1% this year against 12.3% for the S&P 500 and rose 14.7% in the past month alone. Even so, Zacks has moved it to rank 3 (Hold): the estimate-revision trend going into the report was mixed, not the unanimous upgrades of August, the Earnings ESP (-0.04%) is flat, and its industry (Chemical - Diversified) sits in the bottom 18% of Zacks industries, which historically drags on a stock. Expect it to move with the market rather than ahead of it. Next quarter the consensus is $3.48 a share on $3.26 billion of sales, and $14.40 on $13.36 billion for the new fiscal year (up from $13.45 just finished, about +7%). For your 787 shares: hold, keep the $1.81 a quarter dividend coming (about $1,425 gross, roughly $997 net to you), and let your waiting sell order at $327.50 do its work above the year's high of $324. The thing to watch is whether analysts raise the $14.40 in the next few weeks: if they do, the rank improves; if the stock keeps climbing while estimates stand still, it is getting dearer, not better.

gold.label: Gold
gold.nature: Monetary metal — industrial use is only about 5% of demand, so gold is priced almost entirely by macro.

favouring.label: CPI inflation
favouring.why: Metals are bought as an inflation hedge. CPI at 3.7% sits well above the 2% target, which supports that case.

pressuring.label: 10-year REAL yield
pressuring.why: Precious metals pay no income, so the real yield IS the cost of holding them. At 2.91% real (10Y 5.07% minus 2.16% breakeven inflation) that cost is high.

pressuring.label: US dollar (DXY)
pressuring.why: Metals are priced in dollars, so a firmer dollar mechanically pressures them. DXY 103.83, up on the week, up versus its moving averages.

neutral.label: Fed policy rate
neutral.why: Cash competes with metal. A 4.00% policy rate is a moderate hurdle for a non-yielding asset.

neutral.label: Gold speculative positioning
neutral.why: Futures net length is 47.0% of open interest, +2.0 points on the week. Positioning does not cause the move; it shows how crowded the trade already is. Heavy length means a thin cushion, washed-out length means room to run.

neutral.label: Gold price trend
neutral.why: Price is down its moving averages with RSI 21.9. Trend confirms a move, it does not cause one.

silver.label: Silver
silver.nature: DUAL metal — roughly 50-60% of silver demand is industrial (solar PV alone is about 29%, up from 11% in 2014), so factory activity is its demand engine; on top of that it inherits gold’s macro sensitivity in amplified form.

favouring.label: Gold-to-silver ratio
favouring.why: It takes 85.2 ounces of silver to buy an ounce of gold. The long-run band is roughly 60-80: above it silver is historically cheap against gold and tends to catch up; below it silver is the expensive one. At 85.2 silver looks cheap.

favouring.why: Index 103.40, +2.18% year on year and down on the month. Silver is half an industrial metal, so this is its demand engine — solar panels, electronics, EVs and data centres.

KSE100.label: KSE100

regime.verdict: BULL (above the 200-day): the daily trigger alone works -- 79% hit rate, 26% of entries drew down >10%
regime.plain: regime matters more than any indicator: above the 200-day average the daily trigger alone works; below it, evidence must arm first and the trigger must come last

weekly.plain: weekly evidence on the underlying. A-D divergence was the best single component in the test (19 events, 100% positive at 60 days); RSI divergence counts when its first low was at or below 40 (<= 30 never happens on these names)

capitulation.plain: volume at least 2x its 50-day average, close in the lower third of the day near the 20-day low, then an up-day within 5 sessions. Capitulation alone in a bear worked 40% of the time; it counts only with the follow-through

band.label: owner monthly LIP support (coincides with the Oct/Nov-2025 swing lows)

support.plain: the owner band / 52-week low is a zone, not a trigger: it scores only once a weekly close is back above it (present in 70% of the good entries, but 56% alone)

volume.note: no volume on this series at TradingView
volume.plain: after a climax, a retest on shrinking volume (20-day average at 75% of the 50-day or less) is the Wyckoff "test" -- indices only; low-volume single stocks underperform

daily_divergence.plain: daily divergences were the worst input tested (69% of events down more than 10% within 60 days); shown, never scored

trigger.plain: daily trigger on the underlying: reversal candle at the 20-day low, undercut-and-reclaim, or a close above the divergence swing high with RSI above 50. In a bear it must come AFTER the evidence has armed

rule6.plain: rule 6 unchanged: a daily close below the EMA50 (or the breakout level) is a falling knife -- no averaging

KSE100.rule: Bottom Rule v2 (validated on 2021-26 IBKR bars; one real bear, ~20 confirmed events). Step 0 regime = close vs 200-day. Step 1 arm (bear only) = score >= 25 within 14 days: A-D divergence 25, RSI divergence (first low <= 40) 25, capitulation + follow-through 20, support touched + weekly close back above 15, post-climax contraction (indices) 15, daily divergence 0. Step 2 trigger = reversal at the 20-day low / undercut-reclaim / swing-high reclaim with RSI > 50. Bear: CONFIRMED only armed then triggered; PARTIAL = armed, no trigger. Bull: trigger at a higher low into the EMA20/50 band confirms. Rule 6: close below EMA50 = falling knife. KSE-100: provisional until a PSX price history is tested.

Step 2 trigger = reversal at the 20-day low / undercut-reclaim / swing-high reclaim with RSI > 50. Bear: CONFIRMED only armed then triggered; PARTIAL = armed, no trigger. Bull: trigger at a higher low into the EMA20/50 band confirms. Rule 6: close below EMA50 = falling knife.

regime.plain: regime matters more than any indicator: above the 200-day average the daily trigger alone works; below it, evidence must arm first and the trigger must come last

weekly.plain: weekly evidence on the underlying. A-D divergence was the best single component in the test (19 events, 100% positive at 60 days); RSI divergence counts when its first low was at or below 40 (<= 30 never happens on these names)

capitulation.plain: volume at least 2x its 50-day average, close in the lower third of the day near the 20-day low, then an up-day within 5 sessions. Capitulation alone in a bear worked 40% of the time; it counts only with the follow-through

support.plain: the owner band / 52-week low is a zone, not a trigger: it scores only once a weekly close is back above it (present in 70% of the good entries, but 56% alone)

volume.plain: after a climax, a retest on shrinking volume (20-day average at 75% of the 50-day or less) is the Wyckoff "test" -- indices only; low-volume single stocks underperform

daily_divergence.plain: daily divergences were the worst input tested (69% of events down more than 10% within 60 days); shown, never scored

trigger.plain: daily trigger on the underlying: reversal candle at the 20-day low, undercut-and-reclaim, or a close above the divergence swing high with RSI above 50. In a bear it must come AFTER the evidence has armed

rule6.plain: rule 6 unchanged: a daily close below the EMA50 (or the breakout level) is a falling knife -- no averaging

roster: Is this a good business at a fair price?
Is it a solid, durable business?
Is a weak business starting to recover?
Which names do analysts like? Shown as a finder; it does not vote.
Which Pakistani sectors and names suit the macro?
Do the story and the trend agree?
What are the best funds buying?
What do top funds hold that you do not?
Which countries and themes look strong?
Which banks are strong on bank-specific measures?
Is it a good moment to buy (buy now, wait for a dip, avoid)?
Is the trend up, broken or still bottoming?
Is it above its long-term average and not stretched?
Has a falling stock really turned?
Is the whole market near a bottom?
Would the stricter bottom check hold this back?
Is the market in an up or down phase?
Has the 50-day or the ATR stop been broken?
Where are metals and big traders leaning?

master_signal.rule: Business engines say whether the company is attractive; price engines say whether the moment is right; a holding takes the exit arbiter instruction first. BUY needs two business votes and a strong price; BUY SMALL needs one and a positive price; a good business with a weak price is WAIT FOR PRICE.

rules.1: Reversal candle at a level: low touches a support zone, closes green, above the prior day's midpoint, in the upper third of its range. Buy a tranche at the next open; the next session must hold that low or no further tranche.
rules.2: Undercut and reclaim: price trades below a prior swing low intraday but the daily close is back above it (the classic shakeout low).
rules.3: Hourly structure turns: on the 1-hour chart a higher low, then a close above the previous hourly swing high (the intraday version, for a US-session add).
rules.4: Volume signature: the low day prints at least 1.5x the 30-day average volume (capitulation), then the next session is a lighter-volume down day, or an up day on above-average volume.
rules.5: RSI with divergence: daily RSI 30-40 at the touch, and price makes a lower low while RSI makes a higher low (the strongest single signal).
rules.6: Invalidation: a daily close below the base floor breaks the base (no averaging until the next level is tested and confirms by rule 1 or 2). A close below that next level is AVOID.
